sentences.text:
This is an appeal filed by the claimant aggrieved by the Award dated 30.07.2013 passed in M.V.C.No.6431/2011 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bangalore (SCCH-3), whereby the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.3,68,828/-.
NC: 2023:KHC:33867 2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court of Small Causes, Bangalore (SCCH-3)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- and the Tribunal had granted an amount of Rs.3,68,828/-.
The Tribunal held that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation as there was no insurance policy.

The case of the claimant is that on 01.10.2011, at about 9:30 p.m., he was proceeding on a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01/EM- 2764 on 5th Main road, Chamarajpet and when he reached near 4th cross, a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02/EW- 9756 came from behind and dashed against the claimant's vehicle due to the rash and negligent driving of its driver.
Due to the accident, the claimant had sustained grievous injuries and had undergone treatment and spent huge amount and because of the said injuries, he sustained disability also.

3. The Court below on the issue of liability had considered the evidence of RW.1 i.e., the insurer,
RW.2 is the person in whose favour the vehicle was transferred on 26.11.2023.
RW.3 is the person in whose name the NC: 2023:KHC:33867 vehicle was registered as on the date of accident i.e., on 01.10.2011.
According to the original owner, he sold the vehicle and it was transferred on 26.11.2010 and according to the second respondent, as on the date of the accident, he was not the owner of the vehicle.

sentences.text: It is the case of the insurance company that they have not insured the vehicle i.e., motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02/EW-9756.
Basing on this, the Court held that the owner alone is liable and partly allowed the petition.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the insurance company has made a false statement before the Court below that they have not insured the vehicle.

The claimant has filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 of C.P.C., wherein they have filed before this Court a policy issued by the first respondent dated 19.11.2010 to 18.11.2011 and as per that, the registration number is shown as 9758.
In the said policy, the Chassis number is mentioned as 'MD 624 HE 3062L NC: 2023:KHC:33867 79327' and the Engine number is mentioned as 'OE 3L 62079504'.
Learned counsel has also filed the registration extract of the vehicle which is involved in the accident i.e., Reg.No.KA-02/EW-9756.
In that, the Chassis No. is mentioned as 'MD 624 HE 3062L 79327' as is mentioned in the policy.
In the registration extract, another 4 is added to the Engine Number.

Basing on these documents, learned counsel submits that the offending vehicle was insured by the insurance company and the Court below basing on the submission of the insurance company that there is no policy, held that only the owner is liable to pay the compensation.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that consistently it has been the case of the claimant that the Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-02/EW- 9756 is involved.
Now, for the first time, they filed an insurance policy of the vehicle bearing No.9758 and came before the Court stating that this vehicle and the other vehicle is one and the same.

It is submitted that at NC:
2023:KHC:33867 appellate stage, it is not open to the claimant to take such an inconsistent stand.

Alternatively, he submits that if this Court comes to the conclusion that it is one and the same for the first time before the Court, there will be an opportunity to cross examine the claimant on this aspect.
7. This Court has perused the additional evidence placed before this Court.

The Chassis number in the policy as well as in the registration extract and the insurance policy is one and the same and even the Engine number is almost the same except for one additional digit and further, the vehicle number also, instead of 6 in the policy it is shown as 8.

In view of the same, particularly considering the request made by the learned counsel for the insurance company, this Court deems it appropriate to set aside the order impugned and remand the matter back to the Court below and the Court below without any further evidence, basing on the evidence available on record and considering the additional evidence filed before this Court, shall consider by giving an opportunity to the NC:
2023:KHC:33867 insurance company to cross examine the claimant and vice versa.
The Court below shall decide the appeal within a period of two months from the date of receipt of the copy of the order.
Both the parties shall appear before the Court below by 31.10.2023 without any further notice.
8. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed by setting aside the award dated 30.07.2013 and the matter is remanded back for fresh consideration.
